os-core.title: Foundation
os-core.summary: The everyday helpers every other package stands on: text, numbers, results, guards, IDs, paging, modules and secrets.

gives.1: Clean up and convert text, like building a URL slug or reading Persian digits as Latin.
gives.2: Return results and errors in one clear shape instead of throwing exceptions everywhere.
gives.3: Check inputs, make IDs and page through queries with small, focused helpers.

sample.slug: Turn a title into a URL slug

text.title: Text
text.summary: Clean, check and convert strings without null checks everywhere.

1.title: String chores
1.text: `TextEx` gathers the string chores every app repeats.

2.title: Null-safe
2.text: Every method accepts null and returns an empty string or false.

3.title: Chainable
3.text: Nothing throws, so you can chain calls freely.

4.title: Regex helper
4.text: `RegexEx` builds patterns with a cache and a time limit.

1.title: String chores
1.text: `TextEx` covers trimming, slugs, stripping HTML, casing, joining and safe comparisons.

2.title: No exceptions
2.text:
Every method accepts null. It returns an empty string or false instead of throwing.

So you can chain calls freely.

3.title: Regex
3.text:
`RegexEx` adds a cached, time-limited way to build patterns.

It also has a strict email check.

slug.title: Turn a title into a URL slug
slug.note: Accented letters become plain ones, symbols are dropped and spaces become dashes.

clean.title: Strip HTML and shorten it for a preview
clean.note: Each tag becomes a space, so words don't run together. Truncate counts the suffix in the length.

casing.title: Change the casing and join parts
casing.note: Conjoin skips null and empty parts, so no stray separators are left.

checks.title: Check an email, a yes/no answer and a name
checks.note: `ToBoolean` falls back to its default only when it doesn't recognise the answer; "off" is a clear no.

TextEx.IsNull: True when the text is null, empty or only spaces. `IsNotNull` is its opposite.
TextEx.ToSlug: Builds a lowercase, URL-friendly slug. Accented letters become plain ones and Persian letters are kept.
TextEx.Clean: Removes symbols and spaces and lowercases the rest, which is handy for building keys.
TextEx.CleanTags: Removes HTML tags and ` ` and collapses the spaces left behind.
TextEx.Truncate: Cuts the text to a maximum length, suffix included ("..." by default).
TextEx.ToSingleSpace: Collapses repeated spaces into one and trims both ends.
TextEx.TrimIt: Trims spaces and the characters =, - and _ from both ends, and can change the case too.
TextEx.ToLatinDigits: Turns Persian and Arabic digits into 0-9 and leaves everything else as it is.
TextEx.ToBoolean: Reads yes/no answers such as true, 1, on or ✓, including common Persian ones; anything else returns the default.
TextEx.ToCamelCase: `ToCamelCase` joins words split by -, _ or spaces; `ToTitleCase` capitalises each word.
TextEx.IsContain: A case-insensitive Contains that returns false for empty input.
TextEx.IsEqual: Case-insensitive equality; empty text never equals anything.
TextEx.IsPersian: True when every letter is in the Arabic script; spaces, digits and punctuation are skipped.
TextEx.Escape: Escape puts a backslash before quotes, backslashes and control characters; Unescape undoes it.
TextEx.Conjoin: Joins values with a separator and skips the empty ones.

RegexEx.IsEmail: Checks the pattern, then makes sure `MailAddress` reads the address back unchanged.
RegexEx.Create: Builds a regex with a 3-second timeout and caches it; returns null for an invalid pattern.

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.summary: Read numbers from text safely, round them and check ranges.

1.title: No exceptions
1.text: `NumberEx` turns strings and objects into numbers without throwing.

2.title: Bad input
2.text: Bad input gives 0.

3.title: Clamped
3.text: A value too large for the target type is clamped instead of overflowing.

4.title: Digits
4.text: Persian and Arabic digits count as digits when you check text.

1.title: Converting
1.text:
`NumberEx` turns strings and objects into int, long, decimal or double without exceptions.

Bad input gives 0.

2.title: Too large
2.text: A value too large for the target type is clamped instead of overflowing.

3.title: Culture and digits
3.text:
Parsing always uses the invariant culture.

Persian or Arabic digits count as digits when you check text.

parse.title: Read numbers from text
parse.note: Thousands separators are fine; text that isn't a number gives 0 instead of an exception.

round.title: Round and convert without overflow
round.note: Halves round away from zero, and a value too big for int stops at `int.MaxValue`.

checks.title: Check text and ranges
checks.note: Persian digits count as digits, and `IsWithin` includes both ends of the range.

format.title: Percentages and formatted output
format.note: If you don't pass a culture to `ToFormatted`, it uses the current one.

NumberEx.ToInt: Converts text, a double, a long or any object to int. Invalid text gives 0; large values are clamped to int's range.
NumberEx.ToLong: The same safe conversion for the other number types.
NumberEx.ToIntSafe: Returns your default when the value is null.
NumberEx.Round: Rounds halves away from zero, to 2 decimal places by default.
NumberEx.Truncate: Drops the digits after the given precision without rounding.
NumberEx.OrZero: Turns a null int, long, double or decimal into zero.
NumberEx.IsNumber: True when the text holds only digits; Persian and Arabic digits count too.
NumberEx.IsWithin: Checks that a value is in a range, both ends included.
NumberEx.IsEqual: Compares two doubles or decimals within a small tolerance.
NumberEx.IsEven: Checks whether an int is even or odd.
NumberEx.IsInteger: True when a double or decimal has no fractional part.
NumberEx.ToFormatted: Formats a decimal, with N2 and the current culture by default.
NumberEx.ToHex: Writes an int in hexadecimal or binary.
NumberEx.ToByteSafe: Reads a byte (hex by default) and returns the default on bad input.

results.title: Results
results.summary: Return success, failure and data in one shape that both your API and your UI understand.

1.title: Status and code
1.text: `OSResult` carries a status and an optional code and message.

2.title: With data
2.text: `OSResult<T>` adds the data.

3.title: Automatic success
3.text: Succeeded is worked out from the status, never set by hand.

4.title: HTTP codes
4.text: Each status maps to an HTTP code, and exceptions turn into a matching status.

1.title: What it carries
1.text:
`OSResult` carries a status, an optional code and message, field errors and a trace ID.

`OSResult<T>` adds the data.

2.title: Succeeded
2.text: Succeeded is worked out from the status, so you never set it by hand.

3.title: HTTP and exceptions
3.text:
Each status maps to an HTTP code and back.

Exceptions turn into a matching status too, so services can return results instead of throwing.

ok.title: Return data on success
ok.note: Succeeded comes from the status, and Data holds the value.

invalid.title: Report field errors
invalid.note: Invalid maps to HTTP 400, and each `FieldError` says which field failed and why.

from-exception.title: Turn an exception into a result
from-exception.note: The status comes from the exception's type and the code from its name.

json.title: What a result looks like in JSON
json.note: Empty fields are left out, and the status is written in `camelCase`.

type.FieldError: One field's error, with an optional code that programs can read.

OSResult.Ok: A successful result, with or without data.
OSResult.NotFound: There is one factory per status: Invalid, `NotFound`, Conflict, Unauthorized, Forbidden, Failed, Unavailable and Error.
OSResult.Invalid: An invalid result that lists which fields failed.
OSResult.From: Builds a result from an exception: the status from its type, the code from its name.
OSResult.Succeeded: True for Ok, Info, Warning, Existed and `NotExisted`.

OSResult{T}.From: Copies a result's status, code, message and errors into a typed result.

ResultEx.ToHttpStatus: The HTTP status code for a result status, such as 404 for `NotFound`.
ResultEx.FromHttpStatus: The result status for an HTTP code; 429 and 503, for example, both become Unavailable.
ResultEx.ToStatus: Maps an exception to a status, looking through `OSException` wrappers to the real cause.
ResultEx.MessageKey: The translation key for a status, such as `results.notFound`.
ResultEx.FallbackMessage: A plain English message to show when no translation is found.

errors.title: Errors and guards
errors.summary: Stop bad input early, wrap failures with context and report them in one place.

1.title: Argument checks
1.text: Guard checks an argument and hands the value back.

2.title: Your own error
2.text: `OSException` wraps a lower-level failure with your message and code.

3.title: Plain data
3.text: An exception turns into plain data for reporting.

4.title: One sink
4.text: `IErrorSink` is the one place reports are sent.

1.title: Guard
1.text:
Guard checks an argument and hands the value back, so the check fits on the same line as the assignment.

The parameter name is filled in for you.

2.title: Wrapping failures
2.text:
`OSException` wraps a lower-level failure with your own message and code.

Results look through it to the real cause.

3.title: Error reports
3.text:
`ErrorDetail` and `ErrorReport` turn an exception into plain data.

`IErrorSink` is the one place those reports are sent.

check-name.title: Reject empty input
check-name.note: The parameter name is taken from the argument itself, so you never type it.

wrap.title: Wrap a failure without losing its cause
wrap.note: Your message is what people see, while the status and code come from the real cause inside.

detail.title: Turn an exception into readable details
detail.note: Each inner exception is indented under the one that wrapped it.

sink.title: Send reports where you want them
sink.note: Register one sink, and hooks set to Log send their failures to it.

type.OSException: An exception with an optional Code. Without a message, it takes the inner exception's message.
type.ErrorReport: One report with a trace ID, error type, source, route, status code and time.

Guard.NotNull: Returns the value, or throws `ArgumentNullException` with the parameter name.
Guard.NotEmpty: Rejects null, blank text or an empty collection.

ErrorDetail.From: Copies the type, message, `HResult` and stack trace, up to 10 inner exceptions and 8 frames each.
ErrorDetail.ToString: An indented, readable view of the whole chain.

ExceptionEx.Find: Returns the exception itself or the first inner exception of the given type, or null.

ErrorReport.From: Builds a report from an exception: the trace ID from the current `Activity` or a fresh ID, the error type, message and stack trace, and the time from `TimeProvider`.

IErrorSink.TryReport: Where reports go: a log, a database or an outside service.

hooks.title: Hooks
hooks.summary: Let other parts of the app react to an event without the sender knowing about them.

1.title: Any event
1.text: An event is any type you choose.

2.title: Hooks
2.text: Each `IHook<TEvent>` handles the event.

3.title: Priority
3.text: The hook with the higher priority runs first.

4.title: Failure policy
4.text: Each hook decides what happens when it fails.

1.title: Events and hooks
1.text:
An event is any type you choose. Each `IHook<TEvent>` handles it.

`IHookRunner` calls every hook registered for that event.

2.title: Order
2.text:
Highest priority runs first.

Hooks with the same priority keep their registration order.

3.title: When a hook fails
3.text:
Each hook decides what happens when it fails: stop the run, ignore the failure, or report it and carry on.

Cancelling the token always stops the run.

define.title: Write a hook
define.note: A hook is a small class. Priority and `OnFailure` are optional.

register.title: Register the hooks and run them
register.note: Here hooks is the injected `IHookRunner`. `SendReceipt` runs before `UpdateStock` because its priority is higher.

failure.title: Report a failure and carry on
failure.note: The failure is reported with the source `hook:OrderPlaced/AuditHook`, and the next hook still runs. Without a sink, Log acts like Ignore.

type.IHook{TEvent}: One handler: `HandleAsync`, plus Priority (Normal) and `OnFailure` (Throw) when you need them.
type.HookPriority: Named priorities from Highest (200) to Lowest (-200); any other int works too.
type.HookFailure: Throw stops the run, Ignore skips the failure, and Log sends it to `IErrorSink` and carries on.

IHookRunner.RunAsync: Runs every hook for the event in priority order.

HookEx.AddOSHooks: Registers the scoped runner once; calling it again changes nothing.
HookEx.AddOSHook: Registers a hook once (scoped by default), along with the runner.

data.title: Queries and paging
data.summary: Search, sort and page through lists with a few attributes and one page model.

1.title: Search and sort
1.text: Mark properties with `[Searchable]` or `[Sortable]`.

2.title: Any queryable
2.text: `QueryEx` builds search and sort expressions for any `IQueryable`.

3.title: Paging
3.text: `PageInfo` works out Skip, Take and the page count.

4.title: Collection helpers
4.text: `LinqEx` adds a few small helpers for everyday collections.

1.title: Search and sort
1.text:
Mark properties with `[Searchable]` or `[Sortable]`, and `QueryEx` builds the search and sort expressions for any `IQueryable`.

A database provider can turn them into SQL.

2.title: Paging
2.text:
`PageInfo` works out Skip, Take and the page count.

It also keeps the page number in range.

3.title: Collections
3.text: `LinqEx` adds a few small helpers for everyday collections.

page.title: Work out the current page
page.note: Page 99 doesn't exist, so it is pulled back to the last page, 5.

search.title: Search, sort and page a query
search.note: Search first and count after, so the page count matches what was found.

keyset.title: Page by key through long lists
keyset.note: Pass the last ID you showed, and the next 20 rows come back in order.

linq.title: Everyday collection helpers
linq.note: `InsertSorted` keeps the list sorted, so 5 lands between 4 and 9.

type.QueryModel: What a list request carries: Page, Take, Term, `SortName` and `SortType` (1, 10 and Descending by default).
type.PageInfo: Page count, Skip, First, Last and HasMore; a page out of range is pulled back into range. Built without a total (only the rows shown and whether more exist), Total and Count are null.
type.PagingModel{T}: One page of items together with its `PageInfo`.
type.SelectListModel: Simple shapes for dropdown options and key/value pairs.

QueryEx.Search: Keeps the items whose `[Searchable]` text properties contain the term.
QueryEx.OrderBy: Sorts by a `[Sortable]` property, then by the entity key so the order is unique; an unknown name leaves the order as it is.
QueryEx.Paging: Applies the Skip and Take of a `PageInfo`.

PagingEx.PageAfter: Pages by a sorted key instead of Skip, so it stays fast on large tables. With a key and an id, equal keys never skip rows; values are sent as parameters.

LinqEx.HasAny: Checks for items, using Count when the source already knows it.
LinqEx.IsIn: Checks whether a value is one of a few others.
LinqEx.InsertSorted: Inserts into a sorted list with a binary search and skips duplicates.
LinqEx.Loop: Runs an action on each item; `LoopAsync` awaits each one in turn.

ids.title: IDs and keys
ids.summary: Make GUIDs, short codes, random tokens and hashes in one line.

1.title: GUIDs
1.text: `GuidEx` makes GUIDs and reads them from text without exceptions.

2.title: Sequential IDs
2.text: `NewSeqId` gives GUIDs that SQL Server sorts in creation order.

3.title: Tokens and hashes
3.text: `KeyEx` makes secure random tokens and hashes text.

4.title: Numeric codes
4.text: `CodeEx` makes numeric codes, such as a one-time login code.

1.title: GUIDs
1.text: `GuidEx` makes new GUIDs, reads them from text without exceptions and shortens them for URLs.

2.title: Sequential IDs
2.text:
`NewSeqId` gives GUIDs that SQL Server sorts in creation order.

This keeps database indexes tidy.

3.title: Tokens and hashes
3.text:
`KeyEx` makes random tokens with a secure random generator.

It also hashes text with SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512.

4.title: Numeric codes
4.text: `CodeEx` makes numeric codes, such as a one-time login code.

shorten.title: Shorten a GUID for a URL
shorten.note: `ToBase64` is URL-safe and only 22 characters long, and `FromBase64` turns it back into the same GUID.

parse.title: Read a GUID from text
parse.note: Text that isn't a GUID gives `Guid.Empty`, not an exception.

keys.title: A login code, a token and a hash
keys.note: The code always has exactly the digits you ask for (up to 9). The hash is the same for the same text every time.

sequential.title: Give a new row a sequential ID
sequential.note: Use `NewSeqId` for primary keys stored in SQL Server; use `New` everywhere else.

type.CodeEx: Random numeric codes of 1 to 9 digits.
type.GuidEx: Create, read, check and shorten GUIDs.

GuidEx.New: A new random GUID. `NewId` and `FlatId` give it as text, with and without dashes.
GuidEx.NewSeqId: A GUID that SQL Server sorts in creation order. `SeqId` and `SeqFlatId` give it as text.
GuidEx.IsNull: True for `Guid.Empty` or null. `IsNotNull` is its opposite.
GuidEx.IsValid: True when the text is a GUID.
GuidEx.ToGuid: Reads a GUID from text, or returns your default.
GuidEx.ToShort: The first 8 hex characters, for display only, since it isn't unique.
GuidEx.ToBase64: A 22-character, URL-safe form of the GUID.
GuidEx.FromBase64: Turns the `ToBase64` form back into a GUID; throws `OSException` for invalid text.

KeyEx.Unique: 16 random hex characters from a secure random generator.
KeyEx.Stamp: A random Base64 token built from the given number of bytes (20 by default).
KeyEx.To256: The SHA-256 hash as hex, in upper or lower case. Empty input gives an empty string.
KeyEx.ToSHA1: SHA-1 hash. Fine for checksums, not for passwords or anything security-related.

CodeEx.Generate: A random code with exactly this many digits (5 by default, up to `MaxLength`).

objects.title: Objects and enums
objects.summary: Convert loose values, read enum names and descriptions, and create types at runtime.

1.title: Unknown values
1.text: `ObjEx` handles values whose type you don't know yet.

2.title: Convert with To
2.text: It checks for blanks and numbers and converts with `To<T>`.

3.title: Struct and enum
3.text: `ValueEx` checks a struct against its default, and `EnumEx` reads enums safely.

1.title: Unknown values
1.text:
`ObjEx` handles values whose type you don't know yet, such as a cell from a spreadsheet or a value from a settings table.

It checks for blanks and numbers and converts them with `To<T>`.

2.title: Struct and enum
2.text:
`ValueEx` checks a struct against its default value.

`EnumEx` reads enums from text safely and returns the name or description you show users.

3.title: Reflection
3.text:
`ReflEx` creates objects by type.

It also finds a generic interface on a type.

status.title: An enum with display texts
status.note: `Description()` reads the Description attribute and `GetName()` reads DisplayName or Display(Name).

convert.title: Convert a loose value
convert.note: Enums are read by name, ignoring case. A null value gives your default; a value that can't be converted throws `OSException`.

checks.title: Blanks, numbers and defaults
checks.note: An empty GUID counts as blank. `OrDefault` swaps a default value such as 0 for your fallback.

enums.title: Read enums and their display texts
enums.note: With a default, an unknown name returns the default instead of throwing.

create.title: Create a type and find its generic interface
create.note: Constructor errors come back as `OSException` with the original error inside.

type.ObjEx: Checks and conversions for values of unknown type.
type.ValueEx: Compare a value with the default of its type.
type.EnumEx: Read enums from text and get their display texts.
type.ReflEx: Create objects by type and inspect generic interfaces.

ObjEx.IsNull: True for null or for text that is empty or only spaces.
ObjEx.IsBlank: Like `IsNull`, and also true for `DBNull` and `Guid.Empty`.
ObjEx.IsNumeric: True for any number type, or text that reads as a number in the invariant culture.
ObjEx.To: Converts to T using the invariant culture; enums can come from a name or a number.
ObjEx.ToBoolean: Reads yes/no text the same way `TextEx.ToBoolean` does; numbers are true when they aren't zero.

ValueEx.IsDefault: True when the value equals the default of its type, such as 0, false or `Guid.Empty`.
ValueEx.OrDefault: Returns the fallback when the value is its type's default.

EnumEx.ToEnum: Reads an enum by name, ignoring case. Without a default, an unknown name throws `OSException`.
EnumEx.TryParse: Like `Enum.TryParse`, but numbers that aren't defined in the enum are rejected.
EnumEx.Description: The Description attribute, or `GetName()` when there is none.
EnumEx.GetName: DisplayName, then Display(Name), then the member's own name.

ReflEx.Create: Creates an instance with the constructor that matches the arguments.
ReflEx.GetGenericInterface: Finds the closed form of an open generic interface, such as `IRule<decimal>` for `IRule<>`.

modules.title: Modules
modules.summary: Split a large app into modules that register their own services, in dependency order.

1.title: Module
1.text: A module is a class that implements `IModule`.

2.title: Ordering
2.text: `AddOSModules` orders modules so each comes after what it needs.

3.title: Early stop
3.text: A missing module or a cycle stops the registration.

4.title: App info
4.text: `AppInfo` reads the running app's name and version.

1.title: Defining a module
1.text:
A module is a class that implements `IModule`. Its `ModuleInfo` gives a code, a version and the modules it needs.

`Register` adds its services.

2.title: Registering modules
2.text:
`AddOSModules` checks the codes and orders the modules so each one comes after the modules it needs.

It stops on a missing module or a cycle. Then it keeps the list in `ModuleRegistry` so the app can ask which modules are present.

3.title: Repeated libraries
3.text: A library that may be added more than once can use `TryRegisterLib` to register its services only the first time.

4.title: App info
4.text: `AppInfo` reads the running app's name and version.

define.title: Write a module
define.note: The code is 2 to 16 lowercase letters or digits and starts with a letter.

order.title: Register modules and read the registry
order.note: `crm` comes first because `billing` needs it, whatever order you pass them in.

cycle.title: A dependency cycle is caught at startup
cycle.note: Mistakes stop the app when it starts, not later at runtime.

lib.title: Register a library only once
lib.note: The second call returns false, so the services are not added twice.

version.title: Show the app's name and version
version.note: The version comes from the entry assembly; anything after a + in it is dropped.

type.IModule: One module: its `Info` and a `Register` method that adds its services.
type.ModuleInfo: Code, version and dependencies. `Optional` modules come first only when they are present.
type.ModuleRegistry: The registered modules, in the order they were registered.

ModuleEx.AddOSModules: Checks, orders and registers the modules. It can be called only once per app.
ModuleEx.TryRegisterLib: Returns true the first time a library type is seen, and false after that.

ModuleRegistry.Has: True when a module with this code is registered.

AppInfo.Name: The product name from the entry assembly.
AppInfo.Version: The informational version, or the file version when there is none.
AppInfo.NameAndVersion: Name and version together, such as "Shop v1.2.0".

config.title: App configuration
config.summary: Read your app's settings from appsettings, validate them, and stop at startup when a value is wrong.

1.title: Base class
1.text: Inherit from `AppConfigBase`; app code, title and culture come ready.

2.title: Validation
2.text: Limit values with Data Annotations such as `[Range]` or `[Required]`.

3.title: Plain injection
3.text: Inject your config class directly, no `IOptions` needed.

4.title: Early failure
4.text: A bad setting stops the app at startup, not halfway through.

1.title: Ready-made values
1.text:
`AppConfigBase` has three values. `AppCode` is required, up to 50 characters.

`Title` allows up to 200 characters. `Culture` must be a valid culture name.

Keys are written in kebab-case. Use `[ConfigurationKeyName]` on your own properties too, for example `page-size`.

2.title: Registering
2.text:
`AddOSConfig` binds one section to your class and validates it when the host starts.

The class itself is registered too, so take `ShopConfig` straight in a constructor.

3.title: Reading early
3.text:
Sometimes you need settings before the container exists, such as at the top of `Program.cs`. Use `ReadOSConfig` there.

If anything is wrong you get one `OSException` listing every problem.

define.title: The app's configuration class
define.note: Inherit `AppConfigBase` and add only what is yours.

register.title: Register it in the app
register.note: The `shop` section is read and validated.

read.title: Read it right away
read.note: A value you leave out keeps its default; `Title` had nothing, so it is null.

invalid.title: When the configuration is wrong
invalid.note: All problems come together: `AppCode` is missing and `PageSize` is out of range.

type.AppConfigBase: Base class for app configuration with `AppCode`, `Title` and `Culture`.

AppConfigBase.AppCode: Short id of the app; required, up to 50 characters. Its key is `app-code`.
AppConfigBase.Title: Title of the app, up to 200 characters.
AppConfigBase.Culture: A culture name such as `fa-IR`; an invalid name is a validation error.
AppConfigBase.Validate: Checks `Culture`. Override it for more rules and call `base.Validate` too.

ConfigEx.AddOSConfig: Binds one section of the settings to `T`, validates it with Data Annotations (when the host starts) and registers `T` itself.
ConfigEx.ReadOSConfig: Reads that section right now; if it is invalid, throws an `OSException` listing every problem.

scopes.title: Scopes
scopes.summary: Find the closest value for the current company, branch or user, with the whole app as the fallback.

1.title: Scope
1.text: A `Scope` is a kind plus an id, such as branch 42.

2.title: Rank
2.text: Each kind has a rank; higher means more specific.

3.title: Scope chain
3.text: A `ScopeChain` puts the most specific scope first and the app last.

4.title: Reading a setting
4.text: Take the first scope in the chain that has a value.

1.title: What a scope is
1.text:
Some settings and data belong to the whole app, and some to one company, one branch or one user.

A `Scope` is a kind plus an id, such as branch 42. You register each kind with a rank; the higher the rank, the more specific the scope.

2.title: Building the chain
2.text:
`IScopeSource` says which scopes the current request is in.

`IScopeResolver` turns them into a `ScopeChain`: the most specific scope first and the app last.

3.title: Reading a setting
3.text: To read a setting, take the first scope in the chain that has a value.

kinds.title: Register scope kinds and a source
kinds.note: A branch has a higher rank than a company, so it is more specific. Kind 0 is reserved for the app.

fallback.title: Take the closest value
fallback.note: Branch 42 has no currency of its own, so the company's EUR wins over the app's USD.

resolve.title: Get the chain for the current request
resolve.note: Here scopes is the injected `IScopeResolver`. Without any source, the chain only holds the app.

type.Scope: A kind and an id. `Scope.App` is the whole app (kind 0).
type.ScopeChain: Scopes ordered from the most specific to the app, at most one of each kind.
type.ScopeKind: A registered kind: number, code, title key and rank.
type.ScopeRegistry: The registered kinds. Two kinds can't share a code or a rank.
type.IScopeSource: Says which scopes the current request is in, such as the user's company.
type.IScopeResolver: Builds the chain from every registered source.

ScopeEx.AddOSScopeKind: Registers a kind with its code, title key and rank; the rank must be above 0.
ScopeEx.AddOSScopeSource: Adds a source. The resolver asks every source and merges what they return.

ScopeChain.Of: Builds a chain; two different scopes of the same kind throw `OSException`.

secrets.title: Secrets
secrets.summary: Encrypt API keys and passwords before saving them, and tie each one to where it belongs.

1.title: Encryption
1.text: `ISecretBox` encrypts text with AES-GCM.

2.title: Context
2.text: A secret only opens with the same context.

3.title: Your keys
3.text: Keys come from your own `ISecretKeyRing`.

4.title: New keys
4.text: After you add a new key, old secrets still open.

1.title: Encryption
1.text:
`ISecretBox` encrypts a text with AES-GCM.

It returns bytes you can store in the database.

2.title: Context
2.text:
The context, such as `shop:7:payment`, is part of the check. The secret only opens with the same context.

So a value copied to another row or shop won't open.

3.title: Keys
3.text:
Keys come from your own `ISecretKeyRing`, for example from environment variables or a key vault.

The id of the key used is stored with the secret. So after you add a new key, old secrets still open with the old one.

ring.title: Give the app its keys
ring.note: Each key is 32 random bytes. `CurrentKeyId` is the key new secrets are sealed with.

seal.title: Seal a secret and open it
seal.note: Here the box comes straight from the service collection; in an app you inject `ISecretBox`. A different context gives false.

type.ISecretBox: Seals text into bytes and opens it again.
type.ISecretKeyRing: Supplies the encryption keys; you write this for your own key store.

ISecretBox.Seal: Encrypts the text with the current key. Throws `OSException` when the key is missing or isn't 32 bytes.
ISecretBox.TryOpen: Decrypts the bytes; false when the key, the context or the data doesn't match.

SecretEx.AddOSSecrets: Registers `ISecretBox`. Without a key ring, sealing throws a clear error.
SecretEx.AddOSSecretKeyRing: Registers your key ring, replacing any earlier one, together with the box.

reports.title: Reports
reports.summary: Simple shapes for dashboard numbers: counts, totals per group and points on a chart.

1.title: Same shape
1.text: Every module returns dashboard numbers in the same shape.

2.title: Counts
2.text: `ReportCountSet` holds named counts.

3.title: Totals and points
3.text: `ReportGroupAmount` is a group total, and `ReportSeriesPoint` is a chart point.

1.title: Dashboard models
1.text:
These are plain models for the numbers a dashboard shows.

Every module returns them in the same shape.

2.title: Counts and totals
2.text:
`ReportCountSet` holds named counts, such as orders and returns.

`ReportGroupAmount` is a total for one group, such as sales per category.

3.title: Points and ranges
3.text:
`ReportSeriesPoint` is one point on a chart, such as sales in one month.

`ReportRange` names common date ranges for filters.

counts.title: Collect counts for a dashboard
counts.note: Keys ignore case, and a missing key returns null.

monthly.title: Sales per month for a chart

by-category.title: Totals per category
by-category.note: Key is for code and Title is what the user sees.

type.ReportCountSet: Named counts, with keys that ignore case.
type.ReportGroupAmount: A total for one group: Key, Title and Amount.
type.ReportSeriesPoint: One point on a chart: a period and an amount.
type.ReportRange: Common date ranges, such as this week or last year.
type.ReportRangeRequest: A chosen range with its title and dates.
type.MonReportRange: A range given as a number of months.
